name: Cheesy Ground Beef Tortellini
intro_html: Cheese tortellini in a creamy tomato-beef sauce under a blanket of melted mozzarella. It is pasta stuffed with cheese, sauced with cheese, topped with cheese, and somehow still lands at {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories per bowl for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost). We checked the math twice.
ingredients_display: 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 18.75 oz (529 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, dried oregano): ~$0.58. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $37.42 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.67 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $47.75 across 14 servings, roughly $3.41 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.81 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $54.56. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for cheesy beef tortellini that an Italian chain would put on the menu at five times the price with a breadstick as an apology.
shop_smart:
Tortellini is the splurge in this batch, so compare the dry, refrigerated, and frozen versions per ounce; dry store-brand is usually the winner by a wide margin.
One-third fat cream cheese makes the sauce creamy for less money and fewer calories than heavy cream, and the bricks are cheaper per ounce than the tubs.
Store-brand marinara plus cream cheese beats any jarred rosa or vodka sauce on price, and it tastes like you made it on purpose.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground beef in your largest pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains; ground beef should reach 160F. Drain excess fat.
Season with the garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper, then stir in the marinara sauce and bring to a simmer.
Add the cream cheese in chunks and stir until it melts into a creamy rosa-style sauce, 3 to 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the cheese tortellini in salted water until they float and are just tender, then drain.
Fold the tortellini into the sauce gently so they do not tear.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top, cover, and heat on low 3 to 4 minutes until melted. Rest 5 minutes before portioning.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Scoop carefully so each container gets its share of tortellini and sauce. Every bowl comes in at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Brown the ground beef to 160F and drain the fat.
Season, stir in the marinara, and bring to a simmer.
Melt in the cream cheese to make a creamy sauce.
Boil the tortellini until just tender and fold them in gently.
Top with mozzarella, cover until melted, and portion into 14 containers.
